claims.text: The Official Register of the United States 1957 lists 'Lawrence P. Gise' as 'Assistant Director' of the UNITED STATES ATOMIC ENERGY COMMISSION, DIVISION OF MILITARY APPLICATION, legal residence Va 10th, salary 14,190, at printed page 629. The volume states it lists persons in administrative and supervisory positions 'as of May 1, 1957'.

claims.text: The Official Register of the United States 1959 lists 'Lawrence P. Gise' as 'Assistant Director, Administration' of the ADVANCED RESEARCH PROJECTS AGENCY under DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE, legal residence Va 10th, salary 17,500, at printed page 134, under a footnote reading 'Station is Washington, D.C. unless otherwise indicated.' The volume lists positions 'as of May 1, 1959'. The same page lists Roy W. Johnson as Director and William H. Godel as Director, Policy and Planning Division.

claims.source: DNA 6005F, PLUMBBOB SERIES 1957, Defense Nuclear Agency, references 152 and 153, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GOVPUB-D15-PURL-gpo222713/pdf/GOVPUB-D15-PURL-gpo222713.pdf
claims.text: DNA 6005F, the Defense Nuclear Agency's Nuclear Test Personnel Review volume on Operation PLUMBBOB, cites at reference 153 'Gise, L.P., Ass't Director, DMA. [Memo to: R.F. Hertford, Manager, ALOO, Subject: USAF-AEC Agreement on Use of Lookout Mountain Lab at (29-2)-383, w/encl.] Washington, DC: Atomic Energy Commission, DMA. 04/30/57. 29 pages. AT292383.' Reference 152 cites a further Gise memorandum for the Test Manager, subject 'AEC Unofficial Observers', dated 08/27/57.

The same reference list names the Manager of the Albuquerque Operations Office in 1957 as Hertford, at reference 202, 'Hertford, K., Manager, Albuquerque Operations'. Gise's own 1957 memorandum is addressed to that office from AEC headquarters, not written from it.

label: Lawrence P. Gise
narrative: A career federal administrator who sat, two years apart, in the Atomic Energy Commission office that owned military nuclear applications and in the Defense Department's own advanced research agency. The Official Register of the United States, a statutory annual list of federal administrative officers, places him in both. He is named across the Michels podcast corpus as the custodian of material said to have been recovered from a 1962 nuclear test; nothing in any record opened for this node reaches 1962, and the Albuquerque post the corpus assigns him was held by another man in the year his own paper is dated.
